'''Anthony Black''' (born January 20, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class.

==Early life==
Black was born in [[Duncanville, Texas]], to parents Terry and Jennifer.<ref name=feldman>{{cite web |last1=Feldman |first1=Bruce |title=Orlando Magic's Anthony Black 'could out-athlete everybody' as a football prospect |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4634132/2023/06/23/anthony-black-orlanda-magic-nba-draft/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=July 13, 2023 |date=June 23, 2023}}</ref> His mother played [[soccer]] for the [[Texas Longhorns]] and [[Baylor Bears]] while his father played [[college basketball]] for the Baylor Bears and professionally overseas.<ref name=feldman/> When Black was 10 months old, he moved with his family to Germany where his father was playing.<ref name=norlander>{{cite web |last1=Norlander |first1=Matt |title=2023 NBA Draft: Inside Anthony Black's winding journey from bright football future to top-10 pick |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2023-nba-draft-inside-anthony-blacks-winding-journey-from-bright-football-future-to-top-10-pick/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=July 13, 2023 |date=June 22, 2023}}</ref> He became fluent in German by the age of three.<ref name=norlander/> Black moved back to the United States with his mother when it was time for him to begin kindergarten.<ref name=norlander/> His parents separated during his childhood and Black was raised by his mother and step-father, David Peavy, who also coached him in high school.<ref name=norlander/><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/texas/news/duncanville-basketball-star-anthony-black-stays-positive-despite-ongoing-legal-battle-over-eligibility/|title=Duncanville Basketball Star Anthony Black Stays Positive Despite Ongoing Legal Battle Over Eligibility|publisher=[[CBS News]]}}</ref> His younger brother, [[Beckham Black]], is a five-star recruit in the class of 2027 and was the first high school boys basketball player to sign a merchandising deal with ESPN.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/orlando-magic/magic-news-anthony-black-younger-brother-gets-historic-espn-deal |title=Magic guard Anthony Black’s superstar younger brother gets historic ESPN deal
|publisher=Clutch Points|author=Ojeda, Julian|date=June 16, 2026}}</ref>

==High school career==
Black grew up in [[Coppell, Texas]], and initially attended [[Coppell High School]], alongside players such as [[Ryan Agarwal]].<ref name=norlander/> He averaged 16.3 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and two steals per game as a junior and was named second-team all-area.<ref>{{cite web |last=Riddle |first=Greg |date=October 8, 2021 |title=Five-star basketball phenom Anthony Black is ruled ineligible by DEC after transfer to Duncanville from Coppell |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2021/10/08/five-star-basketball-phenom-anthony-black-is-ruled-ineligible-by-dec-after-transfer-to-duncanville/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> Black also played football at Coppell as a wide receiver and caught 78 passes for 1,327 yards and 16 touchdowns over two varsity seasons.<ref name=norlander/> He transferred to [[Duncanville High School]] in [[Duncanville, Texas]] before the start of his senior year.<ref>{{cite web |last=Riddle |first=Greg |date=August 18, 2021 |title=Defending 6A state champion Duncanville adds 4-star basketball recruit Anthony Black from Coppell |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2021/08/18/defending-6a-state-champion-duncanville-adds-4-star-basketball-recruit-anthony-black-from-coppell/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> Black played in only 15 games during his season due to eligibility issues and averaged 13.5 points, 5.8 rebounds, four assists and 2.2 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=March 28, 2022 |title=Anthony Black becomes third 2022 five-star prospect to commit to Arkansas men's basketball team |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33617856 |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

Black was rated a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] after considering offers from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] and [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].<ref>{{cite web |date=March 28, 2022 |title=Anthony Black, 5-star PG, commits to Arkansas |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3501021/2022/03/29/anthony-black-5-star-pg-commits-to-arkansas/ |access-date=November 22, 2024 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> He also considered playing professionally in the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meehan |first=Jim |date=February 10, 2022 |title=Five-star guard Anthony Black trims list to NBA G-League and five schools, including Gonzaga |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/feb/10/five-star-guard-anthony-black-trims-list-to-five-s/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]]}}</ref> Additionally, Black was considered a high-level football recruit and received scholarship offers from Texas, Baylor and Arkansas.<ref name=feldman/>

==College career==
Black entered his freshman season at Arkansas as a starter at guard.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |last2=Cobb |first2=David |name-list-style=amp |date=November 22, 2022 |title=Ranking college basketball's best freshmen: Arkansas' Anthony Black is first Freshman of the Week for 2022-23 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ranking-college-basketballs-best-freshmen-arkansas-anthony-black-is-first-freshman-of-the-week-for-2022-23/ |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> He also entered the season as a potential first-round selection in the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Anthony-Black-Arkansas-NBA-Draft-2022-198780303/|title=Anthony Black has arrived for Arkansas|first=Andrew|last=Ellis|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 27, 2022|access-date=December 1, 2022}}</ref> Black averaged 22 points over three games during the [[2022 Maui Invitational Tournament]] and was named the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Freshman of the Week.<ref>{{cite web |last=Acosta |first=Jonathan |date=November 28, 2022 |title=Arkansas guard Anthony Black named SEC Co-Freshman of the Week |url=https://www.5newsonline.com/article/sports/ncaa/university-of-arkansas/arkansas-guard-anthony-black-named-sec-co-freshman-of-the-week/527-a253ec32-c32b-42bc-a746-fa5b63cebc31 |access-date=December 1, 2022 |website=[[KFSM-TV|5NewsOnline.com]]}}</ref> He was named to the SEC All-Freshman team at the end of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.5newsonline.com/article/sports/anthony-black-ricky-council-devo-davis-sec-honors/527-4fc95e8f-2aab-407e-8d0e-3d9e73c726e0|title=Anthony Black, Ricky Council IV, Devo Davis earn SEC Honors|website=[[KFSM-TV|5NewsOnline.com]]|date=March 6, 2023|access-date=March 21, 2023}}</ref> Black averaged 12.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 2.1 steals per game on the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Black 2022-23 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/anthony-black-1/gamelog/2023 |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> After the season, he announced that he would forgo the remainder of his college eligibility and enter the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Arkansas' Anthony Black, projected top-10 pick, enters NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36169719 |access-date=April 14, 2023 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
The [[Orlando Magic]] selected Black with the sixth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/anthony-black-magic-no-6-pick-2023-nba-draft|title=Anthony Black: Meet the Magic's No. 6 pick in 2023 NBA Draft|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref> He was tied for the second-highest draft pick by an [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] player since the NBA was established in 1949, alongside [[Joe Kleine]], and trailing only former 2x [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year|DPOY]] winner [[Sidney Moncrief]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-23 |title=Black, Smith Go in NBA Draft 1st Rd; Walsh Picked 38th Overall |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/black-smith-go-in-nba-draft-1st-rd-walsh-picked-38th-overall/ |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=Arkansas Razorbacks |language=en-US}}</ref> He was the highest draft pick for a [[Duncanville High School]] player, surpassing [[Greg Ostertag]], who was selected 28th overall in the 1995 NBA Draft, a record that stood until [[Ron Holland (basketball)|Ron Holland]] was selected 5th overall by the Detroit the [[2024 NBA draft|following year]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-20 |title=Duncanville: The Rulers of the Lone Star State |url=https://davesjoint.net/2021/09/20/duncanville-the-rulers-of-the-lone-star-state/ |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=Dave's JOINT |language=en}}</ref>

On December 26, 2023, Black recorded a career-high 23 points and 4 steals in a win against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Orlando Magic vs Washington Wizards Dec 26, 2023 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/orl-vs-was-0022300407 |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> On April 15, 2025, Black recorded 16 points off the bench and shot 3-3 from three point range in a [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]] victory against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] to secure the Magic a spot in the [[2025 NBA playoffs|playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magic 120-95 Hawks (Apr 15, 2025) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401766458 |access-date=2025-07-10 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> 

On November 25, 2025, Black recorded a new career-high 31 points, along with 3 assists off the bench in an [[Emirates NBA Cup]] win over the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Magic 144-103 76ers (Nov 25, 2025) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401809800/magic-76ers |access-date=2025-11-26 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On December 27, he recorded his new and current career high of 38 points in a comeback win against the [[2025–26 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].

==National team career==
Black played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Anthony-Black-Team-USA-gold-medal-FIBA-U18-Americas-Championships-188687100/|title=Anthony Black, Team USA win gold at FIBA U18 Americas Championships|first=Curtis|last=Wilkerson|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=June 13, 2022|access-date=December 1, 2022}}</ref> He averaged 4.7 points, 7.8 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game, helping his team win the gold medal.
